paper.title_en: Optimization of the trigger menu design for the Super Tau-Charm Facility in high-background environments
paper.abstract_en: The Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF) is a new-generation electron-positron collider operating at center-of-mass energies from 2 to 7 GeV, with a luminosity of 0.5 × 10<sup loc="post">35</sup> cm<sup loc="post">−2</sup> s<sup loc="post">−1</sup> at 4 GeV. The high physics event rate and high beam background poses a major challenge to the STCF trigger system. Performance evaluation of the baseline design of the STCF level-1 (L1) trigger menu shows that the background trigger rate increases substantially with the background level. To suppress the background trigger rate, both the charged and neutral trigger channels have been optimized. With these optimized channels, the trigger efficiency remains comparable to that of the baseline design at the nominal background level. Moreover, the trigger efficiency improves by approximately 1.9% for neutral physics processes at five times the nominal background level. The background trigger rate is suppressed by 25% across one to five times the nominal background level, demonstrating that the optimization is sufficient.
